summary.plain: A next-generation gamma-ray observatory being built at two sites, one in Spain and one in Chile, using dozens of telescopes of three different sizes to see the whole sky and the widest range of gamma-ray energies of any single project.
summary.technical: Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory: two-site (La Palma, Spain / Paranal, Chile) imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov array using Large-, Medium- and Small-Sized Telescope classes (up to 4 LST + 23 MST north, up to 23 MST + 37 SST south, per the observatory's own technology page) to cover 20 GeV-300 TeV. Headquarters in Bologna, Italy; Science Data Management Centre in Zeuthen, Germany. Under construction as of the sources fetched this session.

unique_capabilities.value: The next-generation ground-based gamma-ray observatory: two array sites (Northern and Southern Hemisphere) using three telescope size classes (Large, Medium and Small) to cover the widest energy range of any single gamma-ray facility, 20 GeV to 300 TeV.
